thens.text: The cart read through `GET /api/cart` (not the click response) holds exactly one line for B with quantity 1 and unit price P.
The cart page shows B once, quantity 1, price P.
The cart badge shows 1.
After the UI attempt (step 2): `GET /api/cart` holds no line for O and the badge is unchanged.

The wording check: a message or label naming the out-of-stock state is visible on the page (either reading of Q5 satisfies it). The Then asserts only the presence of the text "out of stock" (case-insensitive) on the page (open question Q5, BN-1).
After the API attempt (step 3): the request is not a 2xx and `GET /api/cart` holds no line for O. The exact 4xx code is informative only; R-2 states only "cannot be added".
`GET /api/cart` holds one line for B with quantity 3 and unit price P.
The cart page shows quantity 3 and a line subtotal of 3 x P (P read from the book record, the product is multiplied in the test).
The cart badge shows 3.
Before the click the quantity field holds "3" whole and is still the focused element.
The cart line of B shows unit price equal to the book's price read from `GET /api/books/<id>` (the catalog record), not from the add response.
`GET /api/cart/total` equals 2 x the catalog price (39.98), computed in the test from the catalog price.
The add is accepted for the guest: a 2xx, no redirect to login and no 401.
In the new context with the same cookie `GET /api/cart` holds the line for B quantity 1.
An anonymous context with no cookie sees no line for B (the cart is owned by the cookie). What the guest sees before the first add (empty vs login prompt, BN-9, Q4) is not asserted.

The `Set-Cookie` of the guest add (step 1) is persistent: it carries `Max-Age` or `Expires` in the future, not a session-only cookie that is lost when the browser closes (the persistence clause of R-5).
After login the cart page shows B with quantity 2.
`GET /api/cart` (signed in again) holds the line of B with quantity 2 and no second line for B.
P-zero: a visible message states that the quantity is invalid / must be at least 1.
`GET /api/cart` holds no line for B (nothing added), read after the click completes (message shown or request answered).
The quantity field still shows "0" whole (the UI did not turn it into 1).
For each value a visible message states the quantity is invalid.
`GET /api/cart` holds no line for B after the click completes: not rounded, not coerced to 1.
The field still shows the entered value whole ("-1", "1.5").
A visible validation or error message is shown.
`GET /api/cart` holds no line for B after the click completes.
The field is not silently replaced by a number; its content "abc" is kept whole (a number input may hold an empty value; then the message of Then 1 still appears).
A visible message states the available number (4).

`GET /api/cart` holds no line for B after the request completed. (Whether only the available quantity could be added instead is open question Q2; this Then asserts the requirement text "nothing is added".)
Both second requests are refused (4xx, INSUFFICIENT_STOCK-class error), not a 2xx and not a 5xx.
The line of A still has quantity 3 (not 6, not 5); the line of S still has quantity 1.
Boundary: a third `POST` A quantity 2 (3 + 2 = stock 5) is accepted and the line of A reads 5.

Valid partitions (P-one, P-ten, P-234, P-contains-zero, P-multi-digit, P-stock-boundary): `GET /api/cart` holds one line for B whose quantity equals the entered value exactly (not truncated, not clamped, 234 is not 23 or 2, 100 is not 1) and subtotal is value x P (P from the catalog record).
P-zero: a visible rejection message; no line for B.
P-negative and P-non-integer: a visible rejection message; no line for B (never rounded or coerced to 1).
P-non-numeric: a visible error message; no line for B.
P-above-stock (301): a visible message stating the available number 300; no line for B.
Every invalid partition (P-zero, P-above-stock, P-negative, P-non-integer, P-non-numeric): the cart read via the API after the click completes holds no line for B.
For every partition the typed value stays whole in the field and the field keeps focus until the click (multi-character value entered whole, cleared and re-entered, pasted).
The add is accepted and the line of B has quantity 50 (the stock boundary reading of "maximum allowed"; the 999 schema-cap reading is open question Q3 and is not asserted).
The unit price equals the catalog price P and the total equals 50 x P, computed in the test.
Each request is answered with a 4xx error or the add is capped to a limit that is at most the stock (10): never a 5xx and never a line above stock.
After each request `GET /api/cart` holds either no line for B or one with quantity at most 10.
The application stays up: `GET /api/health` answers 200 and a normal add of quantity 1 for B afterwards is accepted.
Exactly one cart line exists for B (not two) with quantity 5.
The line subtotal equals 5 x P (P from the catalog record).
The cart holds one line per book (three lines for the marked books) with each book's catalog price and the quantities 1, 2, 3.
The total equals p1 + 2 x p2 + 3 x p3, computed in the test from the catalog records.
The answer is 404 with the error code BOOK_NOT_FOUND.
The cart has no line for that bookId and the user's line count is the same as before the request.
In-stock book, each of the three paths: `GET /api/cart` holds a line for the book at the catalog price P (the same price whichever path added it).
In-stock book, each path: the badge increases by the added quantity and a success message is shown.
Out-of-stock book, each path: no line is created (read through the API); the path shows the out-of-stock refusal or does not offer the add.
A second add of the in-stock book by a different path sums into the same single line (quantity 2), never above stock 5.
`GET /api/cart` holds a line for B at the catalog price (the add by the card obeys the add rules of the product page).

If Q6 confirms the present behaviour (now): the line quantity is exactly 1 and the badge rose by 1; if the owner names the earlier behaviour (before), the value follows that answer. No literal is asserted before Q6 is answered.
After step 2 `GET /api/cart` holds a line for W at its catalog price.
If Q6 confirms the present behaviour (now): W is gone from the wishlist (read after the reload of step 5, not from the page state before it); otherwise the owner's rule (before).

If Q6 confirms the present behaviour (now): after the refused move X is still on the wishlist (read after reload) and `GET /api/cart` holds no line for X: no item is lost; otherwise the owner's rule (before).

If Q6 = a (person's answer): G is in the user's cart at quantity 3, equal to the quantity the guest added (the guest item is not lost and the quantity is not coerced to 1); `GET /api/cart` as the signed-in user shows it. Otherwise it follows the owner's answer (before).
If Q6 = a: H has quantity 4 (higher of 2 and 4 wins, not 6); otherwise the owner's rule (before).
If Q6 = a: Z is absent (no stock, dropped) and no line has a quantity above its stock; otherwise the owner's rule (before).
